body.statement: For every \(m\geq1\): if \(K=2\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(C'=C^\top\); if \(K\geq3\), then \(C\sim C'\) if and only if \(C'=C\) or \(\{C,C'\}=\{C_+,C_-\}\). Whenever \(C\not\sim C'\), one has \(d(C,C')\leq3\).
body.justification: This theorem supplies the balanced side of the allocation-balance elbow and an explicit legal separator with at most three heterogeneous units for every inequivalent profile pair.
body.gap: The i.i.d. finite-support product-law criterion of \cite{DutzZhang2026} and the asymptotic fixed-population result of \cite{WuDing2021} do not classify this all-schedule assignment-induced hypergeometric kernel.
body.consumer: DeclareDesign's balanced \(250\)-of-\(500\) binary reply audit can use the exact transpose classification to distinguish a justified histogram symmetry from a sharp-null imputation or an asymptotic HC2 argument.
body.proof_tex:
We first establish the equivalences asserted in the theorem. Reflexivity follows immediately from Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}probability\text{-}equivalence}\). For the binary case, write the response table in the order \(0,1\). Assumption \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}null}\) becomes
\[
 R_{10}-R_{01}=0,
\]
so every legal binary table satisfies \(R=R^{\mathsf T}\). For an arbitrary table, the map
\[
 T_{ab}\longmapsto T^\dagger_{ba}=R_{ab}-T_{ab}
 \tag{1}
\]
is a bijection from \(\mathcal T_R(h,g)\) to \(\mathcal T_{R^{\mathsf T}}(g,h)\): the row sums of \(T^\dagger\) are the control histogram \(g\), and the column sums of \(R^{\mathsf T}-T^\dagger\) are the treated histogram \(h\). Moreover,
\[
 \prod_{a,b}\binom{R_{ab}}{T_{ab}}
 =\prod_{a,b}\binom{R_{ab}}{R_{ab}-T_{ab}}
 =\prod_{a,b}\binom{R^{\mathsf T}_{ba}}{T^\dagger_{ba}}.
\]
Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\text{-}count}\) therefore gives
\[
 W_R(h,g)=W_{R^{\mathsf T}}(g,h).
 \tag{2}
\]
When \(K=2\), the equality \(R=R^{\mathsf T}\), (2), and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}randomization\text{-}kernel}\) imply \(P_R(C)=P_R(C^{\mathsf T})\) for every legal \(R\). Thus \(C\sim C^{\mathsf T}\). For \(K\geq3\), Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}endpoint\text{-}saturation}\) and Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}randomization\text{-}kernel}\) similarly give \(C_+\sim C_-\).

Lemma \(\mathrm{lem{:}transpose\text{-}reduction}\) shows that an equivalence class contains no profile other than \(C\) and \(C^{\mathsf T}\). It remains to show, when \(K\geq3\), that every nontrivial transpose pair other than \(\{C_+,C_-\}\) is separated by a legal table with at most three heterogeneous units. Fix \(C=(h,g)\neq C^{\mathsf T}\), set \(r=h+g\), and let
\[
 S=\{a\in\mathcal A_K:r_a>0\}.
\]
Suppose first that \(S\) contains an interior level. Join two distinct elements of \(S\) unless they are the pair \(\{0,L\}\). The resulting graph is connected, because any interior vertex is adjacent to every other vertex. If
\[
 h_ag_b-g_ah_b=0
 \tag{3}
\]
on every edge, then \(g=r-h\) turns (3) into \(h_ar_b=r_ah_b\). Hence \(h_a/r_a\) is constant on \(S\). Since Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}profile\text{-}space}\) gives \(\sum_a h_a=m\) and \(\sum_a r_a=2m\), that constant is \(1/2\), whence \(h=g\), a contradiction. Thus there are \(a<b\) in \(S\), with \(\{a,b\}\neq\{0,L\}\), for which (3) is nonzero.

Choose \(u,v\in\mathcal A_K\) by
\[
 (u,v)=
 \begin{cases}
 (b-a,0),&a>0,\\
 (b+1,1),&a=0.
 \end{cases}
 \tag{4}
\]
In the second case \(b<L\), so every value in (4) belongs to \(\mathcal A_K\). In both cases \(a+u=v+b\), and the response types \((a,v)\) and \((u,b)\) are heterogeneous. Define
\[
 R_2=D_{r-e_a-e_b}+E_{av}+E_{ub}.
 \tag{5}
\]
The support conditions \(r_a,r_b>0\) make the diagonal filler nonnegative. The table has mass \(2m\), and its two effects sum to \((a-v)+(u-b)=0\), so Assumptions \(\mathrm{ass{:}table\text{-}mass}\) and \(\mathrm{ass{:}weak\text{-}null}\), through Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}legal\text{-}response\text{-}tables}\), make (5) legal. Its heterogeneous count is two by Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}heterogeneous\text{-}count}\).

The four treatment statuses of the two special units yield pooled special outcomes
\[
 e_a+e_u,qquad e_a+e_b,qquad e_v+e_u,qquad e_v+e_b,
\]
respectively. Direct substitution from (4) shows that only the second equals \(e_a+e_b\). Hence only treating the \((a,v)\) unit and controlling the \((u,b)\) unit can complete the diagonal filler to pooled histogram \(r\). By Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\text{-}count}\) and the identities
\[
 \binom{s-1}{t-1}=\frac{t}{s}\binom{s}{t},
 \qquad
 \binom{s-1}{t}=\frac{s-t}{s}\binom{s}{t},
\]
whose denominators here are positive, we obtain
\[
 W_{R_2}(C)=Q_r(h)\frac{h_ag_b}{r_ar_b},
 \qquad
 W_{R_2}(C^{\mathsf T})=Q_r(h)\frac{g_ah_b}{r_ar_b}.
 \tag{6}
\]
We used \(Q_r(g)=Q_r(h)\), which follows coordinatewise from \(g_a=r_a-h_a\) and binomial symmetry. Every factor in \(Q_r(h)\) is positive. Thus (3) and (6) separate the two profiles.

It remains to consider a nontrivial transpose pair supported on \(\{0,L\}\). Write
\[
 h_0=m-i,quad h_L=i,qquad g_0=m-j,quad g_L=j,qquad i\neq j.
 \tag{7}
\]
Both \(r_0\) and \(r_L\) are positive; otherwise the two arm-size constraints would force \(h=g\). Because \(L\geq2\), the table
\[
 R'_2=D_{r-e_0-e_L}+E_{L,1}+E_{0,L-1}
 \tag{8}
\]
is nonnegative, has mass \(2m\), and is legal: its two heterogeneous effects are \(L-1\) and \(-(L-1)\). An endpoint-only observed profile is possible only when both special units are treated, since their control outcomes are interior, including when \(L=2\). The same binomial cancellation as above gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_{R'_2}(C)-W_{R'_2}(C^{\mathsf T})
 &=\frac{Q_r(h)}{r_0r_L}\{h_0h_L-g_0g_L\}\\
 &=\frac{Q_r(h)}{r_0r_L}(i-j)(m-i-j).
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{9}
\]
Thus (8) separates whenever \(i+j\neq m\).

Suppose \(i+j=m\). Then \(r_0=r_L=m\), \(h_0=j\), and \(g_0=i\). If \(i=0\) or \(j=0\), the unordered pair is exactly \(\{C_+,C_-\}\). Otherwise \(i,j>0\); since they are distinct, \(m\geq3\). Define
\[
 R_3=D_{r-2e_0-e_L}+E_{L,0}+E_{0,1}+E_{0,L-1}.
 \tag{10}
\]
The diagonal filler is nonnegative. The three heterogeneous effects sum to
\[
 L-1-(L-1)=0,
\]
so (10) is legal and \(q(R_3)=3\). To yield an endpoint-only profile, the last two special units must be treated because their control outcomes are interior. The first must also be treated: otherwise their pooled observed histogram is \(3e_0\), rather than the missing \(2e_0+e_L\). Thus precisely one special-unit allocation contributes, even for \(L=2\), when the last two response types coincide. Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}assignment\text{-}count}\) gives
\[
 \begin{aligned}
 W_{R_3}(C)
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{h_0(h_0-1)h_L}{m^2(m-1)},\\
 W_{R_3}(C^{\mathsf T})
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{g_0(g_0-1)g_L}{m^2(m-1)},\\
 W_{R_3}(C)-W_{R_3}(C^{\mathsf T})
 &=Q_r(h)\frac{ij(j-i)}{m^2(m-1)}\neq0.
 \end{aligned}
 \tag{11}
\]
All divisions are valid because \(m\geq3\), and the last inequality uses \(i,j>0\) and \(i\neq j\). Equations (6), (9), and (11), together with Lemmas \(\mathrm{lem{:}transpose\text{-}reduction}\) and \(\mathrm{lem{:}endpoint\text{-}saturation}\), prove the complete classification.

We finally verify the uniform separator bound constructively for arbitrary inequivalent \(C=(h,g)\) and \(C'=(h',g')\). If \(h+g\neq h'+g'\), Proposition \(\mathrm{prop{:}diagonal\text{-}reduction}\) separates them with \(D_{h+g}\), because its count for \(C\) is the positive integer \(Q_{h+g}(h)\) and its count for \(C'\) is zero. If the pooled histograms equal \(r\) but \(Q_r(h)\neq Q_r(h')\), the same diagonal table separates them. Both diagonal separators have \(q=0\).

Suppose the pooled histograms and diagonal coefficients agree. Put \(d=h-g\) and \(d'=h'-g'\). For distinct supported \(a,b\), the symmetric switch
\[
 S_{ab}=D_{r-e_a-e_b}+E_{ab}+E_{ba}
\]
is legal, has \(q(S_{ab})=2\), and direct expansion of its two pooled-compatible special allocations gives
\[
 W_{S_{ab}}(C)=Q_r(h)\frac{h_ah_b+g_ag_b}{r_ar_b}
 =\frac{Q_r(h)}{2r_ar_b}\{r_ar_b+d_ad_b\}.
 \tag{12}
\]
The same formula holds for \(C'\). Suppose all off-diagonal products in (12) agree. If \(d=0\), then \(d'_ad'_b=0\) for every \(a\neq b\), so \(d'\) has at most one nonzero coordinate. The balanced arm-size constraints give \(\sum_a d'_a=0\), hence \(d'=0\). If \(d\neq0\), its zero sum gives at least two nonzero coordinates \(p,q\). Their nonzero product makes \(d'_p,d'_q\) nonzero. For any \(a\notin\{p,q\}\), the equality \(d_pd_a=d'_pd'_a\) shows that \(d_a=0\) if and only if \(d'_a=0\). If there is a third nonzero coordinate \(a\), define \(\lambda_c=d'_c/d_c\) on the common support. Product equality gives
\[
 \lambda_p\lambda_q=\lambda_p\lambda_a=\lambda_q\lambda_a=1,
\]
so \(\lambda_p=\lambda_q=\lambda_a\in\{-1,1\}\); comparison with \(p\) gives the same ratio for every other supported coordinate. If \(p,q\) are the only nonzero coordinates, the zero sums give \(d_q=-d_p\) and \(d'_q=-d'_p\), while \(d_pd_q=d'_pd'_q\) gives \((d'_p)^2=d_p^2\). Thus in every case \(d'=d\) or \(d'=-d\). Since \(h=(r+d)/2\) and \(g=(r-d)/2\), this would make \(C'=C\) or \(C'=C^{\mathsf T}\). Therefore, if \(C'\) is neither, some switch (12) separates with \(q=2\). A remaining inequivalent transpose can occur only for \(K\geq3\) and, by the already proved case analysis, is separated by (5), (8), or (10), with heterogeneous count two, two, or three. Definition \(\mathrm{def{:}separator\text{-}size}\) now yields \(d(C,C')\leq3\).
